strategyqa.selection: ChilleD/StrategyQA splits the 2290 labelled StrategyQA examples into train (1603) and test (687); both splits were concatenated in dataset order, train first, giving exactly the 2290 labelled examples. The qid set was verified identical to voidful/StrategyQA strategyqa_train.json (2290 qids). src_idx is the position in that concatenation.
strategyqa.prompt_source: written for this package (not from a published prompt set)
strategyqa.notes: target is lowercase yes/no derived from the boolean `answer` field.

bbh.repo: lukaemon/bbh (six new subtasks) + frozen s26_bbh files (four reused subtasks)
bbh.selection: ten BBH subtasks concatenated in the fixed order date_understanding, logical_deduction_five_objects, tracking_shuffled_objects_three_objects, sports_understanding, boolean_expressions, multistep_arithmetic_two, word_sorting, navigate, causal_judgement, temporal_sequences; idx runs 0..2436 across the file, src_idx is the position within the subtask.
bbh.prompt_source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/suzgunmirac/BIG-Bench-Hard/main/cot-prompts/<task>.txt, canary line and '-----' separator dropped (transformation verified byte-identical against the four already-frozen prompt_bbh_*.txt files)
deviations: causal_judgement has only 187 examples in BBH (identical count in lukaemon/bbh and in the official BIG-Bench-Hard repo bbh/causal_judgement.json), not 250, so the pooled file holds 2437 rows, not 2500. No rows were invented or repeated.

navigate and causal_judgement targets are capitalised 'Yes'/'No' in BBH, not lowercase. They are kept byte for byte as the source has them, which also matches their official CoT prompts ('So the answer is Yes.'). sports_understanding is lowercase 'yes'/'no' in BBH and is likewise unchanged.
gold_text is "" for every BBH row, matching the frozen per-task BBH files.

mmlu.selection: n_s = largest-remainder apportionment of 2000 proportional to each subject's test-set size over the 14042 test rows, ties on the remainder broken by subject name ascending, then a floor of 5 (the floor bound on no subject: the smallest subject has 100 test rows and an exact quota of 14.24). Within each subject the first n_s entries of numpy.random.default_rng(20260908).permutation(N_s) were taken, with a fresh rng per subject. Rows are emitted in subject-alphabetical order, then in the drawn order. src_idx is the row's index in the 14042-row test split; the permutation runs over subject-local positions.
mmlu.prompt_source: written for this package (not from a published prompt set)
mmlu.flan_exemplars: NOT fetched. google-research/FLAN flan/v2/cot_data/ holds only nine CoT source datasets (aqua, creak, ecqa, esnli, gsm8k, qasc, qed, sensemaking, strategyqa) and no MMLU file; Muennighoff/flan has no file matching 'mmlu' or 'cot'; SirNeural/flan_v2's cot_*.jsonl.gz are the same nine datasets. MMLU is a held-out evaluation benchmark in FLAN, so no FLAN MMLU CoT exemplars exist in those sources. The four prompt files are therefore written for this package (not from a published prompt set).
mmlu.mapping_source: the standard MMLU categories.py from hendrycks/test, with its four categories renamed STEM -> stem, humanities -> humanities, social sciences -> social_sciences, 'other (business, health, misc.)' -> other

hellaswag.selection: numpy.random.default_rng(20260908).permutation(10042)[:2000], emitted in the drawn order; src_idx is the drawn validation-split index.
hellaswag.prompt_source: written for this package (not from a published prompt set)
hellaswag.notes: input is '<activity_label>: <ctx>' then 'Which ending is most plausible?' then the BBH Options block; ending texts are verbatim. target is the gold letter derived from the string `label` field ('0'..'3').
